## What this region is

Helpers over a built PrismaMap that split a model's fields into columns (scalar and enum) and relations, and describe each relation's target and collapsed foreign key.

## What it exists for

- Work with a model's column fields rather than its relations
- Find a model's relations and the foreign keys that join them

## How people say these problems

A moment that says any of these, or something close, is this region's. Both voices: the user asking or correcting, and the agent describing what it is about to build.

- which fields of this model are real columns
- drop the included relations from this result
- keep only the column keys of the row
- walk the relations of this model
- which field joins this relation
- follow the foreign key to the parent
- is this a back-relation
- list the real column fields of this model
- walk every relation of this model
- strip the included relations off this record
- work out the foreign key for this one relation field
- I'll filter the model's fields to scalars and enums
- I'll loop the fields and collect the object kinds
- the write result has nested posts, drop them
- I'll zip the from and to fields into a lookup
- which fields are columns, not relations
- which models does this one point to
- I'll delete relation keys from the row by hand
- is this relation a back-relation with no key
- give me the column names in schema order
- list relations with their target and foreign key
- keep only the column keys of this object
- collapse a composite foreign key into a map

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- get the snake_case column name to put in raw SQL → db-identifiers
- read the tree parent tag on a self-relation → annotations
- what does a relation field's type look like in the map → map-shape
- build the map from the Prisma 6 schema file → building-the-map
